#### 1. Glanzmann thrombasthenia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608)

**Proposed mechanism:** FLNA (HGNC:3776) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000924); ITGB3 (HGNC:5898) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation (GO:0001572); ITGA2B (HGNC:5893) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation (GO:0001572); Platelet activation (GO:0001572) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001871); Actin cytoskeleton organization (GO:0030036) —DISRUPTS→ Cell adhesion (GO:0007155); Platelet activation (GO:0001572) —DISRUPTS→ Cell adhesion (GO:0007155). Mutations in FLNA disrupt actin cytoskeleton organization, leading to skeletal abnormalities in terminal osseous dysplasia-pigmentary defects syndrome. Mutations in ITGB3 and ITGA2B disrupt platelet activation, a process dependent on cell adhesion, leading to bleeding tendency in Glanzmann thrombasthenia. Both actin cytoskeleton organization and platelet activation are critical components of cell adhesion, representing a shared pathway convergence.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that FLNA, ITGB3, and ITGA2B function in completely independent cellular pathways with no shared downstream effectors or processes related to cell adhesion. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in FLNA, ITGB3, or ITGA2B associated with normal phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of FLNA, ITGB3, and ITGA2B in cell adhesion pathways could reveal novel therapeutic targets for modulating cell behavior in both skeletal disorders and bleeding conditions, potentially through strategies that enhance or stabilize cell adhesion mechanisms.
